entities.summary: Al-Humaydi, ʻAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, was a renowned Shafi'i jurisprudence scholar and Shaykh of the al-Haram in Medina, Arabia. Born in the 8th century CE, he studied under the great Imam Shafi'i himself, who is considered one of the most influential figures in Islamic jurisprudence. Al-Humaydi's significance lies in his role as a transmitter of Shafi'i's teachings, and his contributions to the development of Shafi'i jurisprudence in the 9th century CE. His work had a lasting impact on the Islamic world, shaping the legal and intellectual landscape of the region for centuries to come. As a testament to his scholarly prowess, al-Humaydi's name is still invoked in Islamic legal scholarship today.
